conservative.read: This conservative plan targets a modest ~1.5% per month, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and lowering concentration. Expect lower volatility and drawdowns, but also more limited upside potential.

balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while maintaining exposure to quality tech. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns, with a balanced approach to potential returns.

plan: Add to SOXL, SPAL, MUU, and METU, increasing leveraged ETF exposure within limits.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4% per month, aiming for stretched growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups. Be aware this raises both upside and drawdown potential; leveraged ETFs decay daily, and losses can be substantial and fast without strict stop discipline.

plan: Sell SOXL, SPAL, MUU, and METU to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETFs.
Sell CRWD and SNOW to zero to reduce high-beta single name exposure.
Add to QQQI, targeting 30% of the book, to prioritize income and yield.
Trim SPY to 20% to meet the single name concentration mandate.
This plan focuses on generating steady monthly distributions with low drawdown.

income.read: This income plan targets ~1% per month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It rotates into income/covered-call ETFs and broad index, cutting leverage and high-beta names. Distributions are variable and NAV can still fall; this is cash-like income, not a savings account, prioritizing low drawdown and reliable income.
